proposals.name: Mineral Atelier
proposals.subtitle: Cobalt, fired clay, moss
proposals.idea: A cool structural blue balanced by warm clay and muted moss. The broad range of hues makes this the most conventional, versatile option.
proposals.use: A conservative all-purpose identity; especially effective for bars and model comparisons.
proposals.caution: Clay and moss lose hue separation in red-green simulations. Keep the square and triangle markers.

proposals.name: Aubergine & Brass
proposals.subtitle: Aubergine, brass, blue spruce
proposals.idea: Deep aubergine supplies the signature; brass adds warmth and blue spruce prevents the system becoming entirely brown or purple.
proposals.use: My first choice for a distinctive research identity: restrained, memorable, and particularly strong in three-series plots.
proposals.caution: Expanded rose and brass shades can converge under simulated color-vision deficiency. Use the three-color core for thin curves.

proposals.name: Oxide & Denim
proposals.subtitle: Oxblood, denim, lichen
proposals.idea: A dark wine-red anchor, softened by washed blue and a yellow-green accent. The materials are familiar; the red-led hierarchy feels different from the current teal.
proposals.use: A warm, grounded alternative with a strong signature for highlighted results and cumulative trends.
proposals.caution: Oxblood and lichen change character in red-green simulations. The lightness difference helps, but markers remain necessary.

proposals.name: Petrol & Rose
proposals.subtitle: Petrol, dusty rose, antique gold
proposals.origin: Soft interior contrasts and material layering
proposals.idea: Petrol and dusty rose share a quiet, softened intensity, with antique gold as a third voice. This is the gentlest evolution of your existing teal-and-earth palette.
proposals.use: A calm editorial identity, well suited to conceptual diagrams, trend areas, and presentation figures.
proposals.caution: Rose and gold can become similar in red-green simulations. Do not identify a series by hue alone.

proposals.name: Ink & Persimmon
proposals.subtitle: Violet ink, persimmon, lake blue
proposals.idea: A dark violet ink anchors warm persimmon and a clear blue. The hue relationships suggest a small print studio, with saturation reduced for precise scientific marks.
proposals.use: The liveliest option: effective for talks, method diagrams, and plots that need a little more visual energy.
proposals.caution: Violet and blue can move closer under red-green simulations. Preserve the circle and triangle shapes; avoid transparent overlaps as category encodings.
